A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LANGSAMP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V1 reports original multilingual pretraining and evaluation results on six downstream datasets, alongside component ablations, embedding visualizations and donor-language experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical study, revises reported results and adds a quantitative comparison of cross-language representation similarity.

M1.justification: The embedding addition, masked-language-modeling objective and downstream procedure remain unchanged. Both versions add language and script embeddings after the Transformer during pretraining and omit them from downstream representation computation.

E1.justification: Glot500-c training and the six downstream datasets retain the same declared language coverage. The new similarity diagnostic reuses SR-B and languages already studied. Additional appendix score entries complete reporting within existing coverage.

E2.justification: The Glot500-m-style baseline, component variants and English-versus-selected-donor comparisons are retained. The new similarity analysis compares the existing baseline and LANGSAMP; newly discussed Adapter approaches are not evaluated.

E3.justification: V2 adds a diagnostic protocol using 100 randomly sampled parallel SR-B sentences in ten languages, eighth-layer mean pooling, subtraction of each language's centroid and pairwise cosine similarity. Existing training budgets, downstream splits and task metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 5.3 and Appendix B directly test the central language-neutrality hypothesis by comparing representations of parallel sentences, with results in Figures 4 and 5. This substantially extends the analysis beyond the retained component ablations, auxiliary-embedding visualization and donor-selection case study.

E5.justification: V2 Table 1 adds standard deviations alongside the averages. V1 already reported five-seed averages, and both versions retain that run count and single-run donor experiments. The PDFs do not establish an increase in runs or additional significance testing.

E6.justification: Taxi1500, NER and POS results are extensively revised in the main and appendix tables. For example, Table 1 baseline/LANGSAMP averages change from 49.4/53.6 to 50.3/53.4 for Taxi1500 and from 71.8/71.7 to 71.5/71.6 for POS. V2 adds nine language-level entries across Tables 8, 9, 11 and 14, plus the similarity findings in Figures 4 and 5. The reason for the revised means is not specified.

T1.justification: The mathematical embedding construction and MLM loss remain equivalent. Neither version supplies formal neutrality guarantees or proofs; the new cosine-similarity diagnostic is an empirical analysis.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that LANGSAMP improves language neutrality and crosslingual transfer, while learned embeddings assist source-language selection. V2 emphasizes new similarity evidence supporting these retained claims without materially redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation and limitations: neutrality is explicitly distinguished from a sufficient or causal explanation of transfer, input-side embeddings are excluded on scope grounds, and gains are distinguished from additional downstream model capacity. It also qualifies the donor-related non-Latin advantage as applying to text classification and adds substantive future directions.

D1.justification: Section 5.3 documents sampling, representation extraction and centroid subtraction for the new diagnostic. Section 4.1 more explicitly distinguishes full-data baseline training from the 5% ablations. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, training duration and code/model access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations and positioning concerning Adapter-based approaches, alignment versus transfer, intermediate-layer neutrality and language grouping, including Pfeiffer et al., Gaschi et al. and GradSim. The central positioning relative to earlier language embeddings and multilingual encoders remains intact; publication updates to existing references are not new works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition and conclusion undergo substantial editing, particularly to clarify pretraining versus downstream use. V2 reorganizes the analysis around a new quantitative subsection, labels source selection as a case study, adds a Future Direction section and expands the appendix structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds similarity heatmaps in Figures 4 and 5, reformats Table 1 to include standard deviations, moves the dataset-information table into Appendix A and places the NER and POS tables on separate pages. The original architecture diagrams, PCA plots and most table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the existing study through a direct similarity diagnostic, uncertainty reporting in Table 1, more complete appendix results and clearer causal limitations. These improve evidential transparency without substantially changing the validation scope. The new diagnostic remains limited to 100 parallel sentences in ten high-resource languages and does not establish that increased neutrality causes better transfer.
